title.en: Volume 268 Biographies 55: Mi Sihan, Gu Badai, Ma Er Han, Tian Liushan, Du Zhen, Sa Mu Ha
title.raw: 卷268 列傳五十五 米思翰 顾八代 玛尔汉 田六善 杜臻 萨穆哈

sentences.zh: 列傳五十五

translations.literal: Biographies 55
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 55

sentences.zh: 米思翰子李榮保顧八代瑪爾漢田六善杜臻薩穆哈

translations.literal: Mi Sihan; his sons; Li Rongbao; Gu Badai; Ma Erhan; Tian Liushan; Du Zhen; Sa Muha
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan; his sons; Li Rongbao; Gu Badai; Ma Erhan; Tian Liushan; Du Zhen; and Sa Muha

sentences.zh: 米思翰，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Manchu.

sentences.zh: 先世居沙濟。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt at Shaji.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Shaji.

sentences.zh: 曾祖旺吉努，當太祖時，率族來歸，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wangjinu, in the time of the Taizu Emperor, led the clan to submit and was appointed niru i jinggin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wangjinu brought the clan over to the founding emperor and was made a company captain.

sentences.zh: 父哈什屯，事太宗，以侍衛襲管牛錄。

translations.literal: His father Hashitun served the Taizong Emperor and, as a bodyguard, inherited management of the niru.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hashitun served Emperor Taizong and, as an imperial guardsman, inherited command of the family company.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部參政，改副理事官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Rites and then changed to associate director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Rites and was later reassigned as associate director.

sentences.zh: 討瓦爾喀，招明總兵沈志祥。

translations.literal: In the campaign against the Walgaha, he induced the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While campaigning against the Walgaha, he persuaded the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang to come over.

sentences.zh: 從攻錦州，明總兵曹變蛟夜襲御營，先眾扞禦，被創，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jinzhou, when the Ming regional commander Cao Bianjiao raided the imperial camp by night, he was first among the troops to resist, was wounded, and fought fiercely to drive the enemy back.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Jinzhou, when Ming commander Cao Bianjiao struck the imperial camp by night, he was the first to meet the assault, took wounds, and fought the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授內大臣、議政大臣，世職屢進一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he was appointed grand secretary and deliberative minister; his hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class adaha hafan with tosaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he became a grand secretary and deliberative minister, and his hereditary rank was repeatedly raised to first-class baron with an additional junior rank.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞攝政，諸大臣鞏阿岱等並附之，哈什屯獨持正，忤睿親王，降世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: When the Prince Regent Dorgon held power, the ministers Gongadai and others all attached themselves to him; Hashitun alone upheld the right, offended the Prince Regent, and was reduced in hereditary rank to baturu hafan.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Regent Dorgon ruled, ministers such as Gongadai sided with him, but Hashitun alone stood firm, crossed the prince, and was demoted in hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 肅親王豪格以非罪死，鞏阿岱等議殺其子富綬，哈什屯與巴哈力持，事乃已。

translations.literal: When Prince Su Haoge died on a false charge, Gongadai and others proposed killing his son Fushou; Hashitun and Bahali held out against it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Su Haoge was put to death on trumped-up charges, Gongadai and others wanted his son Fushou killed, but Hashitun and Bahali objected until the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，累進世職一等阿思哈尼哈番加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took power in person, his hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class ashan i hafan with tosaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shunzhi Emperor assumed personal rule, his hereditary rank was again and again raised to first-class viscount with an additional junior title.

sentences.zh: 十二年，獎奉職恪勤諸大臣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was rewarded among the diligent ministers in office and given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was honored among the dutiful ministers in office and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康熙初卒，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Kangxi reign and was given the posthumous title Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kangxi reign and was posthumously titled Kexi.

sentences.zh: 米思翰，其長子也，襲世職，兼管牛錄，授內務府總管。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan was his eldest son; he inherited the hereditary rank, also managed the niru, and was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan, his eldest son, inherited the family rank, also commanded the company, and was appointed head of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 輔政大臣從假尚方器物，力拒之。

translations.literal: The regent ministers asked to borrow objects bearing the imperial seal; he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the regent ministers sought to borrow imperial regalia, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，知其守正，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Shengzu Emperor took power in person, knowing his uprightness, he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Kangxi Emperor assumed personal rule, recognizing his integrity, he was made vice minister of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢戶部尚書，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to minister of the Board of Revenue and enrolled among the deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was raised to minister of revenue and made a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 是時各直省歲賦，聽布政使存留司庫，蠹弊相仍，米思翰疏請通飭各直省俸餉諸經費，所餘悉解部，由是勾稽出納權盡屬戶部。

translations.literal: At that time the annual levies of each province were allowed to remain in the provincial treasurer's storehouses, and abuses continued in succession; Mi Sihan memorialized requesting a general order to the provinces for salaries and all regular expenses, with the remainder all remitted to the ministry, whereby the power of auditing receipts and disbursements came entirely under the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time each province's annual taxes were left in local treasuries, and corruption went on unchecked; Mi Sihan memorialized that salaries and routine expenses should be met locally while all surpluses were sent to the capital, so that fiscal control passed entirely to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十二年，尚可喜疏請撤籓，吳三桂、耿精忠疏繼入，下戶、兵二部議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Shang Kexi memorialized requesting the abolition of his princedom; Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong memorialized in succession; the matter was referred to the Boards of Revenue and War for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Shang Kexi asked to surrender his fief, and memorials from Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong followed; the case went to the ministries of revenue and war.

sentences.zh: 米思翰與兵部尚書明珠議三籓並撤，有言吳三桂不可撤者，以兩議入奏。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan and the minister of war Mingzhu deliberated that all three fiefs should be abolished together; there were those who said Wu Sangui could not be abolished; the two opinions were submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan and War Minister Mingzhu argued that all three feudatories should be abolished at once, while others held that Wu Sangui's fief could not be touched; both views were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 复集諸大臣廷議，米思翰堅持宜並撤，議乃定。

translations.literal: The ministers were again assembled for court deliberation; Mi Sihan firmly maintained that they should all be abolished together, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: At a further court conference Mi Sihan insisted that all three must go, and the policy was fixed.

sentences.zh: 既而吳三桂反，上命王貝勒等率八旗兵討之，議者謂軍需浩繁，宜就近調兵禦守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wu Sangui rebelled; the emperor ordered princes and beiles to lead the Eight Banners troops to suppress him; deliberators said military supplies would be vast and troops should be mobilized nearby for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, the emperor ordered princes and banner lords to march against him, but some argued that the war would be costly and that nearby troops should be used for defense alone.

sentences.zh: 米思翰言：「賊勢猖獗，非綠旗兵所能製，宜以八旗勁旅會剿。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan said: "The rebels' power is fierce; Green Standard troops cannot control them; the elite forces of the Eight Banners should be joined for joint suppression."
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan said, "The rebels are too strong for the Green Standard Army; we should send the best of the Eight Banners in a combined campaign."

sentences.zh: 軍需內外協濟，足支十年，可無他慮。

translations.literal: Military supplies can be assisted within and without and will suffice for ten years; there need be no other concern.
translations.idiomatic: "With resources pooled from court and provinces, we can supply the war for ten years and need not worry on that score."

sentences.zh: 」於是請以內府所儲分年發給，复綜覈各直省庫金、倉粟，以時撥運，悉稱旨。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he requested that the stores of the inner palace be issued year by year; he also comprehensively audited the gold in provincial treasuries and grain in granaries of each province and arranged timely transport; all accorded with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed issuing supplies from the imperial storehouses year by year, audited provincial silver and grain reserves, and arranged timely shipments—all of which the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「師行所至，屢奉明詔以正賦給軍需，恐有司尚多藉端私派，請敕各督撫嚴察所屬，供應糧餉薪芻，一切動官帑，毋許苛派；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Wherever the army goes, repeated clear edicts have ordered that regular taxes supply military needs; I fear officials still often use pretexts for private levies; I request that each governor-general and governor be ordered strictly to inspect subordinates: provisions of grain, pay, fuel, and fodder should all draw on official funds and private exactions must not be allowed;"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Though repeated edicts say that regular taxes should feed the armies, local officials may still levy illegal surcharges; let every governor-general and governor see that grain, pay, fuel, and fodder come from public funds and that the people are not squeezed."

sentences.zh: 其購自民間者，務視時價支給，勿纖毫累民。

translations.literal: "whatever is purchased from the people must be paid at current prices and must not burden the people in the slightest."
translations.idiomatic: "Whatever must be bought from civilians should be paid at fair market prices, without the least added burden."

sentences.zh: 」上命如議速行。

translations.literal: "The emperor ordered that the proposal be carried out swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered these measures put into effect at once.

sentences.zh: 米思翰尋卒，年甫四十三，上深惜之，予祭葬，諡敏果。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan soon died, aged only forty-three; the emperor deeply regretted it, granted funeral rites, and gave the posthumous title Minguo.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan died soon after, at only forty-three; the emperor mourned him deeply, granted state funeral honors, and posthumously titled him Minguo.

sentences.zh: 時三桂勢方張，精忠及可喜子之信皆叛，議者追咎撤籓主議諸臣，上曰：「朕自少時，以三籓勢日熾，不可不撤。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sangui's power was just expanding, and Jingzhong and Kexi's son Zhixin had all rebelled; deliberators traced blame to the ministers who had chiefly advocated abolishing the fiefs; the emperor said: "From my youth I saw the power of the Three Feudatories growing daily and knew they could not be left standing."
translations.idiomatic: While Wu Sangui was at the height of his power and Geng Jingzhong and Shang Zhixin had also rebelled, critics blamed the ministers who had urged abolishing the fiefs; the emperor said, "Even as a young man I saw the Three Feudatories growing too strong to be left in place."

sentences.zh: 豈因其叛，諉過於人耶？

translations.literal: How could I, because they rebelled, shift the blame onto others?
translations.idiomatic: Am I to blame others because they turned rebel?

sentences.zh: 」及事定，上追憶主議諸臣，猶稱米思翰不置。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the emperor recalled the ministers who had chiefly advocated the policy and still spoke of Mi Sihan without end.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was over, the emperor still spoke again and again of Mi Sihan and the other ministers who had pressed for abolition.

sentences.zh: 米思翰子馬斯喀、馬齊、馬武，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan's sons Maskha, Maqi, and Mawu each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan's sons Maskha, Maqi, and Mawu are each treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 李榮保，襲世職，兼管牛錄，累遷至察哈爾總管，卒。

translations.literal: Li Rongbao inherited the hereditary rank, also managed the niru, was repeatedly promoted to Chahar commandant, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rongbao inherited the family rank, commanded the company as well, rose to Chahar commandant, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，冊李榮保女為皇后，追封一等公。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Qianlong reign his daughter was installed as empress; he was posthumously enfeoffed as first-class duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 his daughter was made empress, and he was posthumously created a first-class duke.

sentences.zh: 十三年，冊諡孝賢皇后，推恩先世，進封米思翰一等公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the empress was given the posthumous title Xiaoxian; favor was extended to former generations, and Mi Sihan was advanced to first-class duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the empress was posthumously titled Xiaoxian; honors reached back to earlier generations, and Mi Sihan was raised to first-class duke.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以李榮保子大學士傅恆經略金川功，敕建宗祠，祀哈什屯、米思翰、李榮保，並追諡李榮保曰莊愨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on account of the merit of Li Rongbao's son, Grand Secretary Fu Heng, in directing the Jinchuan campaign, an imperial order was issued to build an ancestral hall enshrining Hashitun, Mi Sihan, and Li Rongbao, and Li Rongbao was posthumously titled Zhuangque.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, because Li Rongbao's son Grand Secretary Fu Heng had directed the Jinchuan campaign, the court ordered an ancestral hall for Hashitun, Mi Sihan, and Li Rongbao, and Li Rongbao was posthumously titled Zhuangque.

sentences.zh: 顧八代，字文起，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Gu Badai, style name Wenqi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai, whose style was Wenqi, belonged to the Irgen Gioro clan of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父顧納禪，事太宗，從伐明，次大同，攻小石城，先登，賜號「巴圖魯」，予世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: His father Gunazan served the Taizong Emperor, followed in the campaign against the Ming, halted at Datong, attacked Little Stone City, was first to ascend, was granted the title "Baturu," and was given the hereditary rank niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gunazan served Taizong, marched against the Ming, and at Little Stone City near Datong was first up the wall; the emperor named him a Baturu and granted him the hereditary rank of company colonel.

sentences.zh: 旋授甲喇額真。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed jalan i jinggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a battalion captain.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，定陝西、湖南、江南、浙江，皆在行間，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he followed in entering the Pass, and in pacifying Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang was always in the ranks, advancing to third-class adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he crossed into China proper and fought through Shaanxi, Hunan, the lower Yangtze, and Zhejiang, earning promotion to third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 子顧蘇，襲，進二等。

translations.literal: His son Gusu inherited and advanced to second class.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gusu inherited the rank and was raised to second class.

sentences.zh: 顧八代，其次子也。

translations.literal: Gu Badai was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai was his second son.

sentences.zh: 任俠重義，好讀書，善射。

translations.literal: He was chivalrous and valued righteousness, loved reading, and was skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and loyal by nature, loved books, and excelled at archery.

sentences.zh: 以廕生充護軍。

translations.literal: As a yinsheng he served as a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered the guards.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，從征雲南有功，授戶部筆帖式。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, having merit in the Yunnan campaign, he was appointed a clerk of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he distinguished himself in the Yunnan campaign and was made a clerk in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 旋以顧蘇及子佛岳相繼卒，無嗣，顧八代襲世職，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon, as Gusu and his son Foyue died in succession without heirs, Gu Badai inherited the hereditary rank and was transferred to director in the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Gusu and his son Foyue died in turn without heirs, Gu Badai inherited the family rank and was moved to director in the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，聖祖試旗員第一，擢翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, ranked first among bannermen in the Shengzu's examination, he was promoted to reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he topped the emperor's examination of banner officers and was made a Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂陷湖南，遣其將掠兩廣。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui seized Hunan and sent his generals to plunder the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui took Hunan, he sent generals to ravage Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍莽依圖自江西下廣東，駐韶州。

translations.literal: The Pacifier of the South Mangyitu advanced from Jiangxi into Guangdong and encamped at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Mangyitu marched from Jiangxi into Guangdong and camped at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上命顧八代傳諭莽依圖規复廣西，即留軍，從征廣西。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor ordered Gu Badai to convey instructions to Mangyitu to recover Guangxi; he remained with the army and followed the Guangxi campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor sent Gu Badai to tell Mangyitu to recover Guangxi; he stayed with the army and took part in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 巡撫傅弘烈為三桂將吳世琮所敗，莽依圖引兵與相合。

translations.literal: Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shijiong; Mangyitu led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Honglie was beaten by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shijiong, and Mangyitu marched to his relief.

sentences.zh: 顧八代按行諸軍，謂結營散亂，敵至慮不相應。

translations.literal: Gu Badai inspected the various armies and said that their camps were scattered in disorder and that if the enemy came they would fear being unable to support one another.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai inspected the camps and warned that their scattered dispositions would leave them unable to support one another if attacked.

sentences.zh: 世琮兵至，師复敗，還駐梧州。

translations.literal: When Shijiong's troops arrived, the army was again defeated and withdrew to encamp at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijiong attacked, the army was beaten again and fell back to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世琮來追，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shijiong came in pursuit and was driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiong pursued, but they drove him off.

sentences.zh: 顧八代策世琮且復至，益誡備。

translations.literal: Gu Badai judged that Shijiong would come again and urged greater preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai expected Shijiong to return and pressed for tighter defenses.

sentences.zh: 會除夕，世琮以三萬人奄至，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: It happened to be New Year's Eve; Shijiong came suddenly with thirty thousand men and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve Shijiong surprised them with thirty thousand men, and they defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，師進次盤江，與世琮軍遇，莽依圖病甚，以軍事屬顧八代；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the army advanced and halted at Pan River, encountered Shijiong's army; Mangyitu was gravely ill and entrusted military affairs to Gu Badai;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the army reached the Pan River and met Shijiong; Mangyitu was seriously ill and put Gu Badai in command;

sentences.zh: 偕副都統勒貝等渡江，與世琮戰，分兵出敵後，破其左而合擊其右。

translations.literal: together with Vice Commander-in-chief Lebei and others he crossed the river and fought Shijiong, divided troops to strike the enemy's rear, broke their left wing, and joined in striking their right.
translations.idiomatic: he crossed with Vice Commander Lebei and others, sent a detachment around the rebel rear, broke their left, and struck their right in concert.

sentences.zh: 世琮潰​​圍出，遣精騎追之，自殺。

translations.literal: Shijiong broke out of encirclement and fled; elite cavalry were sent in pursuit, and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiong broke out and fled; pursuing cavalry closed in, and he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 師進克南寧，叛將馬承廕與三桂軍合，可十萬，拒戰。

translations.literal: The army advanced and took Nanning; the rebel general Ma Chengbian joined with Wu Sangui's army, numbering about one hundred thousand, and resisted battle.
translations.idiomatic: The army took Nanning, where the rebel Ma Chengbian joined Wu Sangui's forces in a host of some one hundred thousand and offered battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將或難之，顧八代奮入陣，諸將皆力戰，遂破敵。

translations.literal: Some generals hesitated; Gu Badai charged fiercely into the formation, all the generals fought with full strength, and the enemy was broken.
translations.idiomatic: When some generals hung back, Gu Badai charged into the line and roused them all to fight until the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 十八年，京察，掌院學士拉薩里、葉方藹以顧八代從征有績效，注上考；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the metropolitan evaluation, the academicians Lasali and Ye Fangai, on account of Gu Badai's campaign merit, entered him for top grade;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year's metropolitan review, Academicians Lasali and Ye Fangai rated Gu Badai for top honors on account of his campaign record;

sentences.zh: 大學士索額圖改注「浮躁」，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Songgotu changed the entry to "frivolous," and on that account he was deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: but Grand Secretary Songgotu changed the rating to "rash," and Gu Badai lost his post.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖疏言顧八代從征三載，竭誠奮勉，運籌決勝，請留軍委署副都統，參贊軍務，上命以原銜從征。

translations.literal: Mangyitu memorialized that Gu Badai had followed the campaign for three years, exerted himself with full sincerity, and planned for victory; he requested that he remain with the army as acting vice commander-in-chief to assist in military affairs; the emperor ordered him to continue the campaign with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu reported that for three years Gu Badai had served the campaign with tireless zeal and sound strategy, and asked that he stay on as acting vice commander; the emperor let him continue under his former title.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莽依圖卒於軍，顧八代從平南大將軍賚塔下雲南，攻會城。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Mangyitu died in the army; Gu Badai followed the Pacifier of the South Jaisang into Yunnan and attacked the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Mangyitu died in camp; Gu Badai followed General Jaisang into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 顧八代議當先取銀錠山，俯瞰城內，攻得勢。

translations.literal: Gu Badai argued that Silver Ingot Hill should first be taken to overlook the city within and gain the advantage in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai urged taking Silver Ingot Hill first, which overlooked the city and would give the attack its advantage.

sentences.zh: 及勇略將軍趙良棟師至，用顧八代策，先取銀錠山，克會城，雲南平。

translations.literal: When the Valiant and Strategist General Zhao Liangdong's army arrived, Gu Badai's plan was adopted; Silver Ingot Hill was first taken, the provincial capital was captured, and Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When General Zhao Liangdong arrived, they followed Gu Badai's plan, seized the hill, took the capital, and pacified Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 師還，授侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed expositor in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was made a Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，命直尚書房，累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to attend in the Imperial Study and was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he entered the Imperial Study and rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made a ministry director.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，坐事，上責其不稱職，奪官，留世職，仍直尚書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, on account of an offense, the emperor reproached him for not fulfilling his duties, deprived him of office, retained his hereditary rank, and still had him attend in the Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was punished; the emperor said he had failed in office, stripped him of his post but kept his hereditary rank, and still kept him in the Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, on account of illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 顧八代直尚書房時，世宗從受學；

translations.literal: When Gu Badai attended in the Imperial Study, the Shizong Emperor received instruction from him;
translations.idiomatic: While Gu Badai served in the Imperial Study, the future Yongzheng Emperor studied under him;

sentences.zh: 及卒，貧無以斂，世宗親臨奠，為經紀其喪。

translations.literal: when he died, being poor he had no means for burial; the Shizong Emperor came in person to offer libation and arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: and when he died too poor for a proper burial, the prince came in person to mourn and arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，詔复官，加太傅，予祭葬，諡文端，又以其貧，賜其家​​白金萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng an edict restored his office, added Grand Tutor, granted funeral rites, gave the posthumous title Wenduan, and because of his poverty bestowed ten thousand taels of silver on his family.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 his offices were restored, he was made Grand Tutor, granted state funeral honors, and posthumously titled Wenduan; because he had died poor, the court also gave his family ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 八年，建賢良祠京師，諭滿洲大臣當入祀者五人，大學士圖海、都統賚塔，次即顧八代，及尚書瑪爾漢、齊蘇勒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Worthy and Good Shrine was built in the capital; it was announced that five Manchu ministers should be enshrined: Grand Secretary Tuhai, commander-in-chief Jaisang, next Gu Badai, and ministers Ma Erhan and Qisule.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Worthy Ministers Shrine was built in the capital; five Manchu statesmen were named for enshrinement—Grand Secretary Tuhai, Commander Jaisang, then Gu Badai, Minister Ma Erhan, and Qisule.

sentences.zh: 子顧儼，襲世職，自參領官至副都統。

translations.literal: His son Gu Yan inherited the hereditary rank, rising from company adjutant to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu Yan inherited the family rank and rose from company adjutant to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 孫顧琮，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Gu Cong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Gu Cong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾漢，兆佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ma Erhan, of the Zhaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Erhan, of the Zhaojia clan, belonged to the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，繙譯舉人，授工部七品筆帖式，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, as a translator licentiate, he was appointed a seventh-rank clerk of the Board of Works and was repeatedly promoted to vice director in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he passed the translator examination, entered the Board of Works as a seventh-rank clerk, and rose to vice director in the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，陝西提督王輔臣叛應吳三桂，上命揚威將軍阿密達自江寧移師討之，瑪爾漢以署驍騎參領從。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in response to Wu Sangui; the emperor ordered the Expeller of Might Amida to move his army from Jiangning to suppress him; Ma Erhan followed as acting adjutant of the vanguard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, when Shaanxi commander Wang Fuchen joined Wu Sangui's rebellion, General Amida was ordered from Nanjing to suppress him, and Ma Erhan went as acting cavalry adjutant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與副都統鄂克濟哈、穆舒琿等自涇州進兵，屢破壘，斬級數百，克寧州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, together with Vice Commander-in-chief Ekjeha, Mushuhuan, and others, he advanced from Jingzhou, repeatedly broke enemy stockades, beheaded several hundred, and captured Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he marched from Jingzhou with Vice Commanders Ekjeha and Mushuhuan, stormed several rebel forts, took hundreds of heads, and captured Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大將軍圖海督兵圍平涼，輔臣降，瑪爾漢還京師。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Grand General Tuhai supervised troops in besieging Pingliang; Fuchen surrendered, and Ma Erhan returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Grand General Tuhai besieged Pingliang until Fuchen surrendered; Ma Erhan then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 圖海請調涼州、寧夏、固原諸鎮兵進攻興安、漢中，上命副都統吳丹及瑪爾漢赴諸鎮料理徵發，兼詢緩急機宜。

translations.literal: Tuhai requested transferring troops from the garrisons of Liangzhou, Ningxia, Guyuan, and others to attack Xing'an and Hanzhong; the emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Wudan and Ma Erhan to go to the garrisons to manage levies and also to inquire into urgent and leisurely strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhai asked to move troops from Liangzhou, Ningxia, Guyuan, and other garrisons against Xing'an and Hanzhong; the emperor sent Vice Commander Wudan and Ma Erhan to arrange levies and report on strategy.

sentences.zh: 甘肅提督張勇請緩師，上命圖海固守鳳翔、秦州諸要隘，分兵授征南將軍穆佔下湖廣，命瑪爾漢從。

translations.literal: Gansu provincial commander Zhang Yong requested slowing the army; the emperor ordered Tuhai to hold firmly the strategic passes of Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and others, divided troops and gave them to the Conqueror of the South Muzhan to descend into Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Gansu commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance, the emperor told Tuhai to hold Fengxiang and Qinzhou while General Muzhan marched into Huguang, with Ma Erhan in his train.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，穆佔師進貴州，二十年，師進雲南，瑪爾漢皆在行間，得功牌十二。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Muzhan's army advanced into Guizhou; in the twentieth year the army advanced into Yunnan; Ma Erhan was always in the ranks and received twelve merit plaques.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Muzhan entered Guizhou, and in the twentieth the army entered Yunnan; Ma Erhan was with them throughout and earned twelve merit plaques.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，師還，追論徵湖南不力援永興，致損將士，奪功牌九。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified and the army returned, a retrospective deliberation held that in the Hunan campaign he had not vigorously aided Yongxing, causing loss of officers and soldiers, and nine merit plaques were taken away.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was pacified, a review blamed him for failing to relieve Yongxing during the Hunan campaign, costing many lives, and nine plaques were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命巡視河東鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to inspect salt administration east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was sent to inspect salt administration in eastern Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 御史許承宣、羅秉倫劾山西巡撫圖克善令平陽屬十三州縣增報鹽丁加課累民，下巡撫穆爾賽會瑪爾漢覈實，請免虛報一萬七千餘丁。

translations.literal: Censors Xu Chengxuan and Luo Binglun impeached Shanxi governor Tukeshan for ordering the thirteen prefectures and counties under Pingyang to increase reported salt laborers and add levies, burdening the people; the matter was referred to Governor Muerse to join Ma Erhan in verification; they requested exemption of more than seventeen thousand falsely reported laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xu Chengxuan and Luo Binglun accused Shanxi governor Tukeshan of making thirteen counties under Pingyang inflate salt-labor rolls and overtax the people; Governor Muerse and Ma Erhan investigated and asked to strike more than seventeen thousand false entries.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以按治歸化城都統固穆德不實，吏議左遷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, for investigating the commandant of Guihuacheng Gumude as not factual, the personnel office deliberated demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year an investigation of the Guihuacheng commandant Gumude was found unsound, and the personnel office recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授理籓院司務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從大學士索額圖等使鄂羅斯定邊界，辭辨明析，鄂羅斯人折服。

translations.literal: Following Grand Secretary Songgotu and others as envoy to Russia to fix the boundaries, his arguments were clear and discriminating, and the Russians were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: On the border mission to Russia with Grand Secretary Songgotu, his clear reasoning won over the Russians.

sentences.zh: 事聞，聖祖嘉其能。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Shengzu praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the Kangxi Emperor praised his talent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to director in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to director in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷翰林院侍講學士，再遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to reader in the Hanlin Academy, and again promoted to vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he became a Hanlin reader and then vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，命瑪爾漢駐土木董理驛站，以送軍馬羸，吏議奪官，命寬之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to station at Tumu to oversee post stations; because the military horses sent were emaciated, the personnel office deliberated depriving him of office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 the emperor marched against Galdan and left Ma Erhan at Tumu to manage the relay stations. Because the army horses he supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended stripping him of rank, but the emperor showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部尚書，充經筵講官、議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to minister of the Board of War, and served as lecturer at the classics colloquium and deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made minister of war, lecturer at the imperial lectures, and a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，歲饑，流民就食京師。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year there was famine, and refugees came to the capital for food.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year famine drove refugees to the capital for relief.

sentences.zh: 命與內大臣佟國維、明珠、阿密達等監賑。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise relief together with inner court ministers Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to oversee famine relief with inner court ministers Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was moved to the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，以老病乞休。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, on account of old age and illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he retired on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-seventh year, at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 上遣內大臣臨奠，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an inner court minister to offer libation and granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an inner court minister to mourn him and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，世宗諭獎瑪爾漢謹慎忠厚，事聖祖宣力多年，完名引退，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor commended Ma Erhan for prudence and loyalty, serving the Shengzu Emperor with exerted effort for many years, retiring with reputation intact, and posthumously gave him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 the Yongzheng Emperor praised Ma Erhan as prudent and loyal, noted his long service to the Kangxi Emperor and honorable retirement, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賢良祠成，命入祀。

translations.literal: When the Worthy and Good Shrine was completed, he was ordered to be enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Worthy Ministers Shrine was completed, he was ordered enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，高宗命追諡恭勤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor ordered the posthumous title Gongqin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the Qianlong Emperor granted the posthumous title Gongqin.

sentences.zh: 田六善，字兼山，山西陽城人。

translations.literal: Tian Liushan, style name Jianshan, was a native of Yangcheng, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Liushan, whose style was Jianshan, came from Yangcheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授河南太康知縣，時當兵後，勞來安集。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan; the time was just after warfare, and he worked to comfort and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 3 jinshi, he became magistrate of Taikang in Henan and, in the aftermath of war, worked to restore and settle the district.

sentences.zh: 九年，巡撫吳景道疏薦才守兼優，遷戶部主事，監臨清關，复監鳳陽倉兼臨淮關。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Governor Wu Jingdao memorialized recommending him for excellence in both talent and integrity; he was transferred to secretary in the Board of Revenue, supervised Linqing Pass, and again supervised Fengyang Granary concurrently with Linhuai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Governor Wu Jingdao recommended him for combined talent and integrity; he was made a revenue secretary, supervised Linqing Pass, and later Fengyang Granary together with Linhuai Pass.

sentences.zh: 罷濫徵，革奇羨，商民稱便。

translations.literal: He abolished excessive levies and removed irregular surcharges; merchants and commoners praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He ended abusive levies and irregular surcharges, to the relief of merchants and townspeople.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to director.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授江南道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 兵部議禁民乘馬，六善疏言其不便，下廷臣集議，弛禁。

translations.literal: The Board of War deliberated prohibiting common people from riding horses; Liushan memorialized that it was inconvenient; the matter was referred to court ministers for deliberation, and the prohibition was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Board of War proposed banning commoners from riding horses, Liushan argued against it; the court debated the matter and lifted the ban.

sentences.zh: 十六年，疏言：「欲安民在勸清吏，乞敕各督撫實行薦舉，吏部於各督撫蒞任一二年後，列奏薦舉何人，能否察吏安民，即可以是鑑別。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he memorialized: "To settle the people lies in encouraging honest officials. I beg that each governor-general and governor be ordered earnestly to carry out recommendations. After each governor-general and governor has been in office for one or two years, the Board of Personnel should submit a list of whom they recommended and whether they can inspect officials and settle the people — by this one may judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he wrote, "To secure the people we must encourage honest officials. I ask that every governor-general and governor be ordered to recommend them in earnest, and that after one or two years in office the Board of Personnel report whom each has recommended and whether he can judge officials and settle the people — by that we may tell who is fit."

sentences.zh: 議者或謂舉薦清吏，無以處乎不在清吏之列者，一難也；

translations.literal: Some deliberators say that recommending honest officials gives no way to deal with those not among the honest officials — this is the first difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: "Some object that recommending the honest leaves no place for those not on the list — the first difficulty;"

sentences.zh: 恐督撫依舊受賄徇私，二難也；

translations.literal: I fear governors-general and governors will still accept bribes and show favoritism — this is the second difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: "that governors-general and governors may still take bribes and show favoritism — the second difficulty;"

sentences.zh: 徵糧緝逃處分罣礙，三難也。

translations.literal: Penalties for collecting grain and pursuing fugitives create obstacles — this is the third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: "and that grain collection and fugitive-hunting penalties will get in the way — the third difficulty."

sentences.zh: 然臣謂清吏果得薦舉，則為清吏者見公道尚存，益堅其持守，一便也；

translations.literal: Yet your servant maintains that if honest officials truly receive recommendation, then those who are honest officials will see that fairness still exists and will more firmly hold to their integrity — this is the first advantage;
translations.idiomatic: "Yet I hold that if honest men are truly recommended, the honest will see justice still lives and hold firmer to their standards — the first advantage;"

sentences.zh: 群吏以不著清名為愧，力自濯磨，二便也；

translations.literal: Officials as a group will feel ashamed not to have a reputation for integrity and will strive to purify themselves — this is the second advantage;
translations.idiomatic: "that other officials will be ashamed to lack a clean name and will strive to reform — the second advantage;"

sentences.zh: 某省有清吏幾人，以驗政治修廢，三便也；

translations.literal: How many honest officials a province has can test whether governance is well administered or neglected — this is the third advantage;
translations.idiomatic: "that the number of honest officials in a province will show whether its government thrives or fails — the third advantage;"

sentences.zh: 天下曉然知有能必先有守，風俗丕變，四便也；

translations.literal: All under Heaven will clearly know that ability must first have integrity, and customs will greatly change — this is the fourth advantage;
translations.idiomatic: "that the empire will learn that capacity must rest on integrity, and morals will change — the fourth advantage;"

sentences.zh: 向日督撫厭憎清吏無益於己，今必且卵翼而親愛之，五便也。

translations.literal: Formerly governors-general and governors despised honest officials as of no benefit to themselves; now they will surely nurture and cherish them — this is the fifth advantage.
translations.idiomatic: "and that governors-general and governors who once scorned honest men as useless to themselves will now protect and favor them — the fifth advantage."

sentences.zh: 不惑於三難，力致其五便，將循良興起，不讓前古矣。

translations.literal: Not confused by the three difficulties, but striving to achieve the five advantages — then good officials will rise up and not yield to those of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: "Ignore the three difficulties, pursue the five advantages, and worthy officials will rise again, not inferior to those of old."

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministries and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to inspect Changlu salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to inspect the Changlu salt administration.

sentences.zh: 十七年，還掌江南道事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to manage affairs of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he resumed charge of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he asked for leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 三年，補貴州道御史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed censor of the Guizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed censor of the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「兵部議裁山西、陝西、河南等處兵額，三營裁一營。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "The Board of War deliberated cutting troop quotas in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and other places — one camp cut for every three camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he wrote, "The Board of War proposes to cut troop quotas in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and elsewhere, disbanding one camp in three.

sentences.zh: 遇裁之兵，挾久練之技，處坐困之時，窮無所歸，遂為賊盜。

translations.literal: The troops thus cut, possessing long-practiced skills and finding themselves in desperate straits with nowhere to turn, became bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers thus discharged, skilled from long service and stranded in desperate times with nowhere to go, turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 請諭總督、提督諸臣，察已裁之兵，如弓馬嫻熟、膂力精強，仍收入伍。

translations.literal: I request that governors-general, provincial commanders, and other officials be instructed to examine the already-cut troops; those skilled in bow and horse and strong in physique should still be enrolled in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors-general and provincial commanders review discharged men and re-enlist those still adept with bow and horse and strong in body.

sentences.zh: 自後老弱必斥，逃亡不補。

translations.literal: From now on the old and weak must be dismissed, and deserters must not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter only the old and weak should be removed, and deserters should not be replaced.

sentences.zh: 所漸去者疲卒，不慮其為非；

translations.literal: Those gradually removed will be worn-out soldiers — there need be no fear they will do wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Those gradually let go will be worn-out men, and we need not fear they will turn to crime;

sentences.zh: 所招回者勁兵，可資其實用。

translations.literal: Those recruited back will be elite troops who can serve for real use.
translations.idiomatic: those brought back will be strong soldiers of real use."

sentences.zh: 」下部議，令各營汰去老弱，其年力精壯者仍留充伍。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down for deliberation; each camp was ordered to eliminate the old and weak, while those vigorous in years and strength were still retained to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which ordered every camp to weed out the old and weak while keeping vigorous men in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「吏部於往日曾行之事，率皆援以為例，惟意所彼此，莫窮其弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The Board of Personnel, regarding matters previously carried out, generally all cite them as precedents — favoring whichever side they wish, and the abuses are boundless.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The Board of Personnel cites almost every past action as precedent, choosing whichever side suits it, so the abuses never end.

sentences.zh: 請敕部以上所裁定及有旨著為例者，彙為一冊，敬謹遵守，餘仍循舊章。

translations.literal: I request that the ministry be ordered to compile into one volume all determinations made from above and matters expressly ordered to serve as precedent, to be reverently and strictly observed; the rest should still follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all rulings from above and all matters expressly made precedent be compiled in one volume and strictly followed, while everything else remains under the old rules."

sentences.zh: 」得旨，如所請。

translations.literal: " The imperial response granted approval as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 七年，命巡視京、通倉，還掌山東道事，得旨內升，回籍待缺。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the Beijing and Tongzhou granaries; he returned to manage affairs of the Shandong circuit; received imperial approval for internal promotion and returned to his native place to await a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he inspected the Beijing and Tongzhou granaries, resumed charge of the Shandong circuit, received approval for promotion from within the ranks, and returned home to await appointment.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授刑科給事中，秩視正四品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Penalties Section, with rank equal to regular fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made supervising secretary of the Penalties Section, with the rank of a regular fourth-grade official.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「臣里居讀上諭，以蘇克薩哈為鼇拜仇陷，殺其子孫，連坐族人白爾赫圖，恩予昭雪。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your servant, reading at home the imperial pronouncement that Suksaha was framed by Oboi's faction, his descendants were killed, and his clansman Bierhetu was implicated, and grace was granted to clear their names.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "At home I read Your Majesty's edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi's faction had framed, whose descendants were killed, and whose clansman Bierhetu was implicated along with him.

sentences.zh: 臣思法律為天下共者也，以滿洲勞苦功高之人，因與執政諸臣意見相左，輒牽連興大獄，恐尤而效之，報復相尋，藉端推刃。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that law is what all under Heaven shares. That Manchus who had toiled and achieved high merit, because their views differed from those of the ruling ministers, were immediately implicated in major cases — I fear others will take this as a warning and imitate it, revenge will follow in succession, and pretexts will be found to draw the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Law belongs to all the realm alike. When meritorious Manchus who had borne hardship were dragged into great cases because they differed with those in power, others may copy the example, revenge may run on, and any pretext may become a blade.

sentences.zh: 周禮有八議，罪大可減，罪小可赦。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou has the Eight Deliberations — great crimes may be reduced, small crimes may be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou provides the Eight Deliberations: great crimes may be mitigated and lesser ones pardoned.

sentences.zh: 請特製昭示，滿洲犯罪非反叛有實蹟者，一準於律，勿妄議株連。

translations.literal: I request a special edict be issued making clear that when Manchus commit crimes without actual evidence of rebellion, the law alone shall apply — do not recklessly discuss implicating others.
translations.idiomatic: I ask for a special edict declaring that Manchus guilty of crimes short of proven rebellion shall be judged by law alone, without reckless talk of implicating others.

sentences.zh: 儲人才，固國本，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Storing talent and securing the foundation of the state lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: On this depends the preservation of talent and the security of the state."

sentences.zh: 」上韙其言，下王大臣議，從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words, referred the matter to princes and ministers for deliberation, and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial, referred it to princes and ministers, and agreed.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「聖學宜先讀史。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Imperial learning should first read history.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Imperial study should begin with history.

sentences.zh: 史者，古帝王得失之林也。

translations.literal: History is the forest of gains and losses of ancient emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: History is the record of what ancient rulers gained and lost.

sentences.zh: 其君寬仁明斷，崇儉納諫，則其民必安，其事必治，其世必興必平。

translations.literal: If the ruler is broad-minded, benevolent, and decisive, honors frugality and accepts remonstrance, then the people will surely be at peace, affairs will surely be well governed, and the age will surely rise and be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is generous, clear-minded, frugal, and open to remonstrance, the people are secure, affairs are well ordered, and the age flourishes.

sentences.zh: 若夫苛察因循，惡聞過，樂逞欲，其民必不安，其事必不治，其世必衰必亂。

translations.literal: As for being harsh and scrutinizing, following old ways, hating to hear of faults, and delighting in indulging desires — the people will surely not be at peace, affairs will surely not be well governed, and the age will surely decline and fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When he is harsh, nitpicking, resentful of criticism, and given to his desires, the people are uneasy, affairs go untended, and the age declines into disorder.

sentences.zh: 乞諭日講諸臣，以通鑑與經史並進。

translations.literal: I beg that the daily lecture ministers be instructed to advance the Comprehensive Mirror together with the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the daily lecturers be instructed to teach the Comprehensive Mirror alongside the classics and histories."

sentences.zh: 」得旨俞允。

translations.literal: " The imperial response granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋轉戶科掌印給事中。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 三遷至右僉都御史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏言：「吳三桂負恩叛逆，處必滅之勢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized: "Wu Sangui betrayed his grace and rebelled; he is in a position that must be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he wrote, "Wu Sangui has betrayed imperial grace and rebelled; he stands in a position that must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 綠旗月餉，步兵一兩有奇，馬兵二兩有奇，甲胄不必堅強，弓刀不必精利，登山涉水，資以先驅。

translations.literal: Green Standard monthly pay: foot soldiers slightly over one tael, cavalry slightly over two taels; armor need not be strong, bows and blades need not be sharp — they mount hills and cross waters to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard troops receive a little over one tael a month for infantry and two for cavalry; their armor need not be the finest nor their weapons the sharpest — they are meant to climb hills, ford streams, and lead the way.

sentences.zh: 臣謂綠旗力雖弱，善用之則強；

translations.literal: Your servant maintains that though Green Standard strength is weak, used well it becomes strong;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that though the Green Standard Army is weak in itself, used well it can be strong;

sentences.zh: 心雖渙，善收之則聚。

translations.literal: though hearts are dispersed, gathered well they coalesce.
translations.idiomatic: though their spirit is scattered, gathered well it can unite.

sentences.zh: 供給宜足，勞逸宜均。

translations.literal: Provisions should be sufficient; labor and rest should be balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Their supplies should be adequate and their burdens fairly shared.

sentences.zh: 至先登破陣，無分滿、漢，賞賚公平。

translations.literal: As for being first to ascend and break formations, without distinction between Manchu and Han, rewards should be fair.
translations.idiomatic: For leading assaults and breaking enemy lines, Manchu and Han alike should receive fair rewards.

sentences.zh: 斯忠勇自奮，克佐勁旅以奏膚功，今日所宜急計者也。

translations.literal: Then loyalty and courage will spontaneously arise, and they can assist elite forces to achieve ordinary merit — this is what should be urgently planned today.
translations.idiomatic: Then loyalty and courage will rise of themselves, and they can help the main forces win real victories — this is what must be planned at once."

sentences.zh: 」下部議鼓勵綠旗官兵敘給爵賞例。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the ministry, which deliberated regulations for encouraging Green Standard officers and soldiers with enfeoffment and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which drafted rules for rewarding Green Standard officers and soldiers with titles and honors.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，疏言：「臣昔為河南知縣時，孫可望、李定國尚據云、貴、四川，其勢不減於吳三桂。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he memorialized: "When your servant was formerly magistrate in Henan, Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo still held Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan — their power was no less than Wu Sangui's.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he wrote, "When I was magistrate in Henan, Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo still held Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan — a threat no smaller than Wu Sangui's today.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛江西，姜瓖叛大同，亦不異耿精忠、王輔臣。

translations.literal: Jin Shengheng rebelled in Jiangxi, Jiang Xiang in Datong — this was no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shengheng rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong — no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.

sentences.zh: 而當日民心未若今之驚惶疑懼者，由其時督撫有孟喬芳、張存仁、吳景道諸臣，敦行儉樸，慎守廉隅，吏治肅清，民生樂遂也。

translations.literal: Yet the popular mind of that day was not so frightened and fearful as today, because at that time among governors-general and governors were such ministers as Meng Qiaofang, Zhang Cunren, and Wu Jingdao — earnest in conduct, frugal and plain, carefully guarding integrity, with administration cleared, and the people's lives content.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people then were not so panic-stricken as now, because governors such as Meng Qiaofang, Zhang Cunren, and Wu Jingdao were frugal and upright, kept administration clean, and let the people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 宜特頒嚴諭，令各督撫禁雜派，覈軍實。

translations.literal: It is fitting to specially issue a stern edict ordering each governor-general and governor to prohibit miscellaneous levies and verify military strength.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict should go out ordering every governor-general and governor to stop irregular levies and verify troop strength.

sentences.zh: 有司或剝民敗檢，立行糾劾，以省民力、安眾心。

translations.literal: If any official extorts the people or fails in integrity, immediately impeach and investigate, to save the people's strength and settle popular minds.
translations.idiomatic: Any official who squeezes the people or breaks discipline should be impeached at once, to spare the people and steady their hearts.

sentences.zh: 師行所至，更宜審酌剿禦。

translations.literal: Wherever the army goes, it is still more fitting to deliberate carefully on suppression and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the army marches, commanders should weigh carefully how to suppress rebels and protect the people.

sentences.zh: 近見江西、浙江報捷諸疏，屢言殺賊累萬。

translations.literal: Recently seeing victory reports from Jiangxi and Zhejiang, they repeatedly speak of killing rebels by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Recent victory reports from Jiangxi and Zhejiang repeatedly claim tens of thousands of rebels killed.

sentences.zh: 然必待殺盡而後入閩，恐愚頑之民無盡，草竊之賊亦無盡。

translations.literal: Yet if one must wait until all are killed before entering Fujian, I fear the foolish and stubborn people are endless, and grass-thief bandits are also endless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we must kill every last man before entering Fujian, the foolish and the petty bandits will never run out.

sentences.zh: 臣謂先取精忠，則群賊自息。

translations.literal: Your servant maintains that if one first takes Jingzhong, then the band of rebels will naturally subside.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if we take Geng Jingzhong first, the other rebels will subside of themselves.

sentences.zh: 昔姜瓖乍叛，土寇群起，瓖滅，土寇亦盡，其明驗也。

translations.literal: In former times when Jiang Xiang first rebelled, local bandits rose in groups; when Xiang was destroyed, the local bandits also ended — this is clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Xiang first rebelled, local bandits rose everywhere; when he fell, they vanished too — clear proof of the point.

sentences.zh: 至三桂狡謀，覬以一隅之地困天下全力，我即以天下全力困此一隅。

translations.literal: As for Sangui's cunning scheme, hoping to use one corner of land to exhaust the full strength of the empire — we should use the full strength of the empire to exhaust this one corner.
translations.idiomatic: As for Sangui's scheme to tie down the empire with one corner of the realm, we should tie down that corner with the full strength of the empire.

sentences.zh: 三桂授首，則四川、廣西不煩兵而自定。

translations.literal: When Sangui's head is delivered, then Sichuan and Guangxi will pacify themselves without troubling the army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sangui is dead, Sichuan and Guangxi will settle themselves without further fighting."

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「臣籍山西，與陝西接壤。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Your servant's native place is Shanxi, bordering Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "My native province is Shanxi, which borders Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 黃河自邊外折入內地，至蒲州一千餘裡。

translations.literal: The Yellow River turns from beyond the border into the interior, more than a thousand li to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River enters the interior from beyond the frontier and runs more than a thousand li to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒲州上至禹門，為平陽府屬，河西為西安，有提督、總兵重兵駐守。

translations.literal: From Puzhou up to Yumen, belonging to Pingyang Prefecture — west of the river is Xi'an, where provincial commander and regional commander heavy troops are stationed.
translations.idiomatic: From Puzhou up to Yumen, in Pingyang Prefecture, the west bank faces Xi'an, where provincial and regional commanders keep heavy garrisons.

sentences.zh: 自此以北，永寧州、臨縣為汾州府屬，渡口有孟門鎮、高家塔諸處；

translations.literal: From here northward, Yongning Prefecture and Lin County belong to Fenzhou Prefecture; at the crossings are Mengmen town, Gaojia Tower, and other places;
translations.idiomatic: North of that, Yongning Prefecture and Lin County belong to Fenzhou Prefecture, with crossings at Mengmen, Gaojia Tower, and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 更北保德州為太原府屬，渡口有黑田溝、窮狼窩諸處。

translations.literal: Further north, Baode Prefecture belongs to Taiyuan Prefecture; at the crossings are Heitiangou, Qionglangwo, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: farther north, Baode Prefecture belongs to Taiyuan Prefecture, with crossings at Heitiangou, Qionglangwo, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 河西為延安，素稱荒野，河東為交城，路險山深，草竊潛匿。

translations.literal: West of the river is Yan'an, always called wilderness; east of the river is Jiaocheng, paths dangerous and mountains deep, where grass-thief bandits hide.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river lies wild Yan'an; east of it lies Jiaocheng, where steep roads and deep hills hide petty bandits.

sentences.zh: 請敕巡撫、提督分兵駐防。

translations.literal: I request that governors and provincial commanders be ordered to divide troops for garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors and provincial commanders be ordered to post troops at these crossings."

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「師已抵平涼，輔臣迫於必死，困獸猶鬥，殺賊百不償失兵一。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "The army has already reached Pingliang; Fuchen, driven to certain death, fights like a cornered beast — killing a hundred rebels is not worth losing one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The army has reached Pingliang. Fuchen, with no way out, fights like a cornered beast; killing a hundred rebels is not worth the loss of one of our men.

sentences.zh: 宜駐軍城下，以逸待勞，急攻固原，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: One should encamp the army below the city, wait at ease for the weary enemy, urgently attack Guyuan, and cut off their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: We should camp beneath the walls, wait at ease for his exhaustion, strike Guyuan hard, and cut his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 平涼地瘠，非比湖南地廣米多，可以持久。

translations.literal: Pingliang's land is barren, unlike Hunan with broad territory and abundant rice — one cannot endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang is poor country, unlike Hunan with its broad fields and abundant grain; the enemy cannot hold out long.

sentences.zh: 糧道不通，人心自散，必有斬輔臣獻軍門者。

translations.literal: When the grain route is cut, hearts will naturally scatter, and there will surely be someone who beheads Fuchen and presents him at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once supplies fail, his followers will scatter, and someone will surely cut off Fuchen's head and bring it to camp.

sentences.zh: 若賊東出則東應，賊西出則西應，疲我師徒，分我威力，固原圍解，賊氣貫通，此斷斷不可者也。

translations.literal: If when rebels go east we respond east, when rebels go west we respond west — exhausting our troops, dividing our power, relieving the siege of Guyuan, and connecting rebel morale throughout — this is absolutely not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If we chase east when the enemy moves east and west when he moves west, we will exhaust our troops, split our strength, lift the siege of Guyuan, and let rebel morale revive — that must not be allowed."

sentences.zh: 」諸疏並下王大臣議行。

translations.literal: " All the memorials were together sent down to princes and ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these memorials were referred to princes and ministers and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以夏旱求言，疏言：「今日官至督撫，居莫敢誰何之勢，自非大賢，鮮不縱恣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in response to summer drought requesting opinions, he memorialized: "Today officials reaching governor-general and governor occupy a position where none dare challenge them; unless one is a great worthy, few do not indulge and act arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when drought prompted a call for advice, he wrote, "Governors-general and governors now stand where no one dares challenge them; unless a man is truly exceptional, few resist excess.

sentences.zh: 道府歲納規禮，加之以搜括，則道府所轄官民，不啻鬻之道府矣。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants and prefectures pay yearly customary gifts; added to this is squeezing — then the officials and people under circuit intendants and prefectures are little different from being sold to circuit intendants and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants and prefects pay yearly gifts upward, and on top of that squeeze their jurisdictions — so the officials and people under them are virtually sold to their superiors.

sentences.zh: 州縣歲納規禮，重之以勒索，則州縣所屬士民，不啻鬻之州縣矣。

translations.literal: District magistrates pay yearly customary gifts; compounded with extortion — then the gentry and people under district magistrates are little different from being sold to district magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: District magistrates pay gifts to prefects and add extortion of their own — so the gentry and common people under them are virtually sold to their magistrates.

sentences.zh: 世祖朝，山東巡按程衡劾巡撫耿焞，江南巡按秦世禎劾土國寶，皆置重典，天下肅然。

translations.literal: In the reign of the Shizu Emperor, Shandong surveillance commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan surveillance commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao — all received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shunzhi Emperor, Shandong surveillance commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun and Jiangnan commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao; both offenders received severe punishment, and the empire was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 今巡按久停，雖欲議复，恐一時難得多人。

translations.literal: Today the surveillance commissioners have long been suspended; even if we wish to discuss restoring them, I fear it would be difficult to find enough men all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissioners have been suspended for so long that even if we debated restoring them, we could hardly find enough qualified men at once.

sentences.zh: 惟有出自上意，欲清一省，則選一人遣往，不必一時俱發。

translations.literal: Only if it comes from the emperor's own intent, wishing to cleanse a province, should one man be chosen and sent — there is no need to dispatch them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the emperor himself wishes to cleanse a province should a single man be chosen and sent; there is no need to launch them all together.

sentences.zh: 出其不意，示以不測，使天下奸惡吏不敢恃督撫而肆志，即有不肖之督撫，亦莫敢庇貪而害民。

translations.literal: Strike when least expected, show unpredictability, so that wicked officials throughout the realm dare not rely on governors and governors-general to indulge their will; even if there are unworthy governors or governors-general, none would dare shield the greedy and harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Strike without warning and keep officials guessing, so that corrupt clerks everywhere dare not lean on their governors for impunity — and even unworthy governors dare not shelter the greedy at the people's expense.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and noted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 調戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，疏言：「國家有錢法以通有無、利民用，自秦、漢及唐、宋，公私皆悉用錢；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he memorialized: "The state has a coinage system to circulate goods and benefit the people; from Qin and Han through Tang and Song, public and private alike all used coin;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he wrote, "The state maintains coinage to move goods and serve the people. From Qin and Han through Tang and Song, public and private alike used cash;

sentences.zh: 至金、元，以銀與錢鈔並行；

translations.literal: under Jin and Yuan, silver circulated alongside paper notes and coin;
translations.idiomatic: under Jin and Yuan, silver circulated with notes and coin;

sentences.zh: 至明中葉，乃專資於銀。

translations.literal: by the mid-Ming, silver alone became the standard.
translations.idiomatic: by mid-Ming, the empire relied on silver alone.

sentences.zh: 闖逆之亂，或沉江河，或埋山谷，又以貪吏厚藏，銀益少，民益困。

translations.literal: During the chaos of the rebel Li, some was sunk in rivers, some buried in valleys, and corrupt officials hoarded heavily — silver grew scarcer and the people more destitute.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Li Zicheng's rebellion, silver was lost to rivers and buried in hills, while grasping officials hoarded still more — supply shrank and the people grew poorer.

sentences.zh: 今欲救天下之窮，惟有多鑄錢。

translations.literal: To relieve the empire's poverty today, there is no remedy but to mint more coin.
translations.idiomatic: To relieve the empire's want today, nothing will serve but to mint more coin.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢所資，銅六鉛四，而可采之山，所司每深諱之，蓋恐時有時無，貽累償稅。

translations.literal: Coin requires six parts copper and four parts lead; yet the offices responsible for mineable mountains deeply conceal them, fearing that when output fluctuates they will be burdened with compensating taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Coinage needs six parts copper to four of lead, yet the offices that oversee mineable hills conceal them, fearing that when yields fluctuate they will be held liable for tax shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 且上官聞其地開採，此挾彼制，誅求甚多也。

translations.literal: And when superiors hear of mining in a region, they use one office to control another and extort heavily.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors hear that a place has opened mines, they play one office against another and squeeze the region dry.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜令天下產銅鉛之地，任民採取，有則以十分二輸稅於官，無則聽之州縣自行稽察，毋使多官旁撓。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that wherever copper and lead are produced, the people should be allowed to mine; when there is output, two-tenths shall be paid to the state as tax; when there is none, let the prefectures and districts inspect on their own, and do not let multiple officials interfere from the side.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that wherever copper and lead occur, the people be free to mine; when ore is found, two-tenths should go to the state, and when none is found, let prefectures and districts inspect on their own — without a swarm of officials meddling from the side.

sentences.zh: 報採多者予議敘，則官與民皆樂為，資以鼓鑄，錢不可勝用矣。

translations.literal: Those who report large yields should be considered for promotion — then officials and people alike will gladly work, supply coinage, and cash will be more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: Reward those who report rich yields with promotion, and officials and commoners alike will gladly supply the mint — coin will be more than enough."

sentences.zh: 」下九卿詳議，擬例以上，得旨：「採銅關係國計，其令各督撫率屬殫力奉行。

translations.literal: " It was referred to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation; regulations were drafted and submitted, and the imperial reply said: "Mining copper concerns the national economy; let each governor and governor-general lead his subordinates to devote full effort to enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Nine Ministers; after deliberation a regulation was submitted, and the emperor replied, "Copper mining bears on the national economy — let every governor and governor-general lead his subordinates to enforce this with all diligence.

sentences.zh: 六善以老病乞罷，上不許。

translations.literal: Liushan pleaded retirement on grounds of age and illness; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Liushan asked to retire on grounds of age and illness, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒於家，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he died at home, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died at home, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 杜臻，字肇餘，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Du Zhen, courtesy name Zhaoyu, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen, whose courtesy name was Zhaoyu, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，改庶吉士，散館，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, completed his term, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, completed his probation, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was promoted to vice minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 國初以海上多事，下令遷東南各省沿海居民於內地，畫界而設之禁。

translations.literal: Early in the dynasty, because of trouble at sea, an order was issued to relocate coastal residents of southeastern provinces inland, demarcating a boundary and imposing restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, with the coast in turmoil, the court ordered coastal populations of the southeastern provinces moved inland, drew a boundary, and imposed strict prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 界外皆棄地，流民無所歸，去為盜。

translations.literal: Land beyond the boundary was abandoned; displaced people had nowhere to go and turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Land beyond the line was left empty; displaced people with nowhere to go turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 及師定金門、廈門，總督姚啟聖請以界外地按籍還民，弛海禁，收魚鹽之利給軍食，廷臣持不可。

translations.literal: After the army captured Kinmen and Xiamen, Governor-General Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned to the people by registry, maritime restrictions lifted, and profits from fishing and salt applied to army provisions — court ministers held this inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: After Kinmen and Xiamen were taken, Governor-General Yao Qisheng asked that abandoned coastal land be returned to its registered owners, sea bans eased, and profits from fish and salt applied to army rations — but court ministers opposed the plan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，台灣平，上命以界外地還民。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, after Taiwan was pacified, the emperor ordered that land beyond the boundary be returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22, once Taiwan was pacified, the emperor ordered coastal land beyond the boundary returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 會給事中傅感丁請以江、浙、閩、粵濱海界外地招徠開墾，乃命臻及內閣學士席柱赴福建、廣東察視展界，進臻工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the supervising secretary Fu Ganding requested that abandoned coastal land in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong be opened for settlement, the emperor ordered Zhen and Grand Secretary Xi Zhu to proceed to Fujian and Guangdong to inspect the extension of the boundary; Zhen was promoted to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Fu Ganding proposed opening abandoned coastal land in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong, the emperor sent Zhen and Grand Secretary Xi Zhu to Fujian and Guangdong to inspect the boundary extension and promoted Zhen to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 臻與席柱如廣東，自欽州防城始，遵海以東而北，歷府七、州三、縣二十九、衛六、所十七、巡檢司十六、台城堡砦二十一，還民地二萬八千一百九十二頃，復業丁口三萬一千三百。
